login.description: Sign in to the sensor's panel.
login.resetHint: Holding the BOOT button for 10 s restores it.
start.description: Presence from the mmWave radar plus the room's temperature, humidity and light.
start.soundHint: Beeps by distance – the closer the person, the faster
sensors.title: Nearby
sensors.description: All Whisli Sense sensors on this network. The panel connects to each one directly; there is no main sensor.
sensors.searching: Looking for sensors on the network…
sensors.graphHint: Click a card to open that sensor's panel. The faster the dashes flow, the better the Wi-Fi signal.
sensors.name: Sensor
radarSettings.description: Where the radar looks for people, how long it waits before the room counts as empty, and how sensitive each zone is.
radarSettings.calibrationHint: The wizard fits the thresholds to this room: you leave for under a minute while the sensor measures the noise, then sit where you usually sit while it measures your breathing. It takes about 1.5 minutes. Run it after mounting the sensor or when presence drops while someone sits still.
range.zoneHint: The radar measures distance in 70 cm gates. Targets closer than “from” or farther than “to” are ignored, e.g. objects right next to the sensor or the hallway behind the door.
range.delayHint: A shorter timeout clears presence sooner, but a person sitting still may disappear. 0–600 s.
sensitivity.description: The bar shows movement and breathing in a gate, and presence lasts while the bar reaches the line. Drag a line to change that gate's threshold: left – more sensitive, right – fewer false detections. Only gates inside the detection range are shown.
sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
sensitivity.footnote: Blue gate – the radar sees a target there. Gates up to 1.4 m have a lot of the radar's own noise, so the thresholds are high there. When you sit still, your bar has to reach the line, or presence ends after the timeout.
sensitivity.noiseLine: Red line – the empty room's noise from calibration.
sensitivity.factoryMessage: All gates go back to a new radar's values. The calibration result is lost.
sensitivity.noEnergy: The radar sends no data – the bars are not current.
sensitivity.footnote: Blue gate – the radar sees a target there. Gates up to 1.4 m have a lot of the radar's own noise, so the thresholds are high there. When you sit still, your bar has to reach the line, or presence ends after the timeout.
calibration.description: The radar sees movement, but also noise: a fan, a curtain, reflections from walls and furniture. Calibration measures how much of that noise your room has and puts the lines just above it, so nothing but people switches presence on. Then it checks how clearly your breathing shows while you sit, so presence does not drop while you read or watch a film.
calibration.tip1: The sensor should already be where it will stay. Calibrate again after moving it or the furniture.
calibration.tip2: Leave the room as it usually is: if a fan usually runs or a curtain moves, keep it that way – calibration should learn it.
calibration.tip3: Take pets out and close the door. Nobody may enter the room during the first 50 s.
calibration.tip4: Take your phone with this panel along, or leave the computer with sound on – the signals tell you when to come back.
calibration.total: About 1.5 minutes in total. The sensor times the steps and saves the thresholds itself; the panel plays sound signals.
calibration.step.leaveText: After clicking Start you have a moment to leave and close the door.
calibration.step.emptyText: The sensor records the highest noise in each gate and puts the lines half as high again.
calibration.step.backText: Three rising tones = come back. Sit where you usually sit, e.g. on the sofa or at the desk.
calibration.step.stillText: You sit calmly and breathe normally. The sensor measures your breathing and lowers the line in your gate. A chord at the end = done.
calibration.now.leave: Leave now and close the door
calibration.now.leaveText: Measuring the empty room starts in a moment.
calibration.now.empty: Stay out – measuring the empty room
calibration.now.emptyText: You will hear three rising tones when you can come back.
calibration.now.backText: The noise lines are saved already. Sit where you usually sit – measuring your breathing starts by itself or when you click “I'm sitting”.
calibration.now.stillText: Breathe normally and don't move. You will hear a chord at the end.
calibration.seesSomething: The radar sees something at {distance}. If nobody is in the room, that is noise – calibration takes it into account.
calibration.notSeen: The radar does not see you now – sit within the sensor's range.
calibration.doneTitle: Done – thresholds saved in the radar
calibration.foundYou: I see you in gate {gates} – the line there sits between the noise and your breathing. In the other gates the lines sit just above the empty room's noise. You can move any of them later in Radar → Settings.
calibration.notFound: Your breathing did not stand out from the noise in any gate, so the noise-only thresholds stay. Check that the radar points at you and nothing blocks it, then calibrate again.
calibration.outside: Gate {gates} is outside the detection range – the radar ignores it. Change the range in Radar → Range.
calibration.tableHint: “Noise” – maximum in the empty room, “you” – the level your breathing exceeded 80% of the time. Struck out – thresholds before the calibration.
calibration.undone: Thresholds from before the calibration restored.
settings.description: The sensor's name, the panel password and firmware updates.
settings.name: Name
settings.nameHint: Shown in the panel, the sensors overview and Home Assistant. The network address is made from it.
settings.passwordHint: Protects the panel and the API. Scripts sign in with HTTP Basic (whisli:<password>). Holding BOOT for 10 s restores the default password.
settings.defaultPassword: You are using the default password – change it.
led.description: What the coloured LED on the board shows. Changes show at once.
led.mode.distanceHint: Blinks while someone is there – faster the closer they are, like a parking sensor.
led.mode.presenceHint: Lit while someone is in the room.
led.mode.statusHint: Dark while all works. Blinks only on a problem.
led.mode.offHint: Never lit (except the BOOT button password reset).
led.alertsHint: Blue blink every 2 s – no Wi-Fi, red every 3 s – a sensor fault. They take priority over the mode.
led.darkOffHint: When the room is dark (below 5 lx) the LED stays off, so it does not bother at night.
firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.hint: Upload a firmware.bin file. The sensor saves it and restarts; settings stay.
firmware.restartMessage: The sensor will be unavailable for a few seconds.
firmware.uploaded: Firmware saved, the sensor is restarting.
firmware.waiting: Waiting for the sensor to come back…
firmware.notBack: The sensor did not come back within a minute. Check its power and network.
network.description: The Wi-Fi connection and the access point for the first setup.
network.apHint: Turns on by itself when the sensor has no Wi-Fi for a minute. The panel is then at http://192.168.4.1/.
network.wifiHint: The network the sensor joins. Pick it from the list or type its name.
network.connectHint: After changing the network the sensor gets a new IP address. If it cannot connect, it opens the access point after a minute.
network.forgetMessage: The sensor disconnects from {ssid} and opens the access point {ap}.
network.apPasswordHint: Password of the {ssid} network. Default: whisli_gogo.
network.apDefaultPassword: The access point uses the default password – change it.
mqtt.description: Home Assistant over MQTT. The sensor works the same without a broker.
mqtt.connectionHint: The sensor connects to an MQTT broker – usually the Mosquitto add-on in Home Assistant – and announces itself there.
mqtt.baseTopicHint: Start of this sensor's topics. Leave empty for the default.
mqtt.discoveryPrefixHint: Where Home Assistant looks for devices. Usually “homeassistant”.
mqtt.discovery: Announce the sensor in Home Assistant (MQTT Discovery)
mqtt.topicsHint: Home Assistant creates the entities itself: occupancy, distance, temperature, humidity, illuminance and Wi-Fi signal.
mqtt.topicState: state as JSON: occupancy, distance, temperature, humidity, lux, rssi
diagnostics.description: Sensor and chip status – useful when something does not work.
logs.description: The sensor's latest events (up to {capacity}). The log lives in RAM – a restart clears it.
log.radarFailed: Radar did not take the settings · {detail}
log.calibrationDone: Calibration done · gates with a person: {detail}
log.calibrationUndone: Thresholds from before the calibration restored
error.tooSoon: Too fast – try again in a moment.
error.radarNotReady: The radar has not answered yet – try again in a moment.
error.invalidSsid: Enter the network name (up to 32 characters).
error.invalidTopic: Topic: no #, + or empty levels, up to 64 characters.
error.noReply: The radar does not answer commands.
problem.radarSilent: The radar sends nothing – check its power and the TX/RX wires.
problem.radarSettings: Could not read or write the radar settings.
problem.sht30: The temperature and humidity sensor (SHT30) does not answer.
problem.bh1750: The light sensor (BH1750) does not answer.
problem.mqtt: No connection to the MQTT broker.
sensorError.noResponse: no answer on the I²C bus
sensorError.noAck: the sensor did not acknowledge a command
mqttError.credentials: The broker rejected the user or password.
mqttError.unreachable: Cannot reach the server – check the address, port and network.
calibrationError.cancelledAfterNoise: Calibration stopped – the thresholds from the empty room stay.
calibrationError.noEnergy: The radar sent no energy data.
calibrationError.tooFewSamples: Too few measurements with the person.
